title.narrative: Supporting communities in creating proper living conditions for IDPs and evacuees at collective centers

description.narrative: ltpgtThe project's primary objective is to enhance the safety, dignity, and well-being of internally displaced persons (IDPs) and evacuees in Ukraine, specifically targeting collective sites in Kirovohrad and Cherkasy regions. This will be achieved through coordinated site management, increased access to essential services, and community engagement.ltbrgtTo improve living conditions, the project will strengthen camp management practices to ensure that collective sites meet minimum safety and dignity standards. Regular assessments and infrastructure improvements will be implemented to make these environments more secure and habitable for IDPs and evacuees. Additionally, site managers and local partners will receive targeted training in camp coordination, equipping them with the skills needed for effective management and emergency preparedness within these sites.ltbrgtThe project will promote community engagement by establishing two-way communication channels within these collective sites, providing IDPs and evacuees a platform to express their needs, voice feedback, and participate in decision-making processes related to their care. These feedback mechanisms will enable service providers to tailor responses more closely to community needs, fostering a stronger sense of trust and accountability in collective sites.ltbrgtA key focus is expanding access to protection services for IDPs and evacuees residing in collective sites, especially in underserved areas. Mobile multi-functional teams will visit these sites regularly, offering services such as case management, legal aid, and social support tailored to the needs of the displaced population. This approach ensures that evacuees and IDPs at remote or less accessible collective sites are included in the service provision network.lt/pgt
